answer: A useful anti-sybil mechanism is a refundable stake bond: before an agent can claim rewards, it locks a deposit slashed if peers later prove its work fake. One honest identity is cheap, but a tide of fake identities means locking a deposit for each one, so attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents pay nothing net. Verification runs in tiers, like a terrace: cheap automated checks first, then costly peer review only for disputed claims. A jetty of public evidence, signed work logs anyone can audit, makes fake claims easy to challenge, so sybils bleed deposits instead of profiting.
